scenario: 你在设计一个 Dynamo 风格的 key-value store，调用方想把头像原图、视频片段和小型会话状态都直接塞进 value。
scenario_en: You are designing a Dynamo-style key-value store, and clients want to store profile images, video chunks, and small session state directly as values.
q: KV store 该如何处理大 value？
q_en: How should the key-value store handle large values?
options: 把大对象放进 blob store，value 里只存对象引用
把所有 value 都拆成固定 4KB 页并由 KV 层重组
要求调用方只用关系表存大对象
把大 value 复制到每个存储节点以减少跳转
options_en: Store large objects in a blob store and keep only a reference in the value.
Split every value into fixed 4 KB pages and reassemble them inside the KV layer.
Force clients to store large objects only in relational tables.
Replicate large values to every storage node to avoid extra hops.
optionMeanings: KV 层只保存小元数据和指针。
KV 层承担对象分块与重组。
把对象存储问题推给 RDBMS。
每个节点都保存完整大对象。
optionDirectness: 适合 KB 到 MB 级元数据访问。
适合你要做文件系统而不是 KV 索引时。
适合强事务对象模型而不是按 key 查 blob。
只适合极小只读配置，不适合大对象。
optionScenarioImpacts: KV 节点避免被视频读写拖垮。
KV 层复杂度和网络放大都会上升。
主键读优势被关系存储成本抵消。
存储和复制成本按节点数膨胀。
why: 我会把大对象放到 blob store，KV value 只留 URL 或对象 ID。KV store 的强项是按主键快速定位小值，大对象会放大复制、修复和网络成本。
why_en: I would keep large payloads in blob storage and store only a reference because the KV layer should stay optimized for small primary-key values.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标本来就是分布式文件系统，固定分块和重组才可能成为主路径。
tradeoff: KV 快速主键访问 vs 大对象传输成本

termDefinitions.meaning: blob store 是面向大二进制对象的存储，通常通过对象 ID 或 URL 访问。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A blob store keeps large binary objects and exposes them through an object ID or URL.

scenario: 一个服务主要按 userId 读取会话、购物车和偏好设置，不需要 join、复杂过滤或跨行事务。
scenario_en: A service mostly reads sessions, carts, and preferences by userId, with no joins, complex filters, or cross-row transactions.
q: 为什么 KV store 比 RDBMS 更贴合？
q_en: Why is a key-value store a better fit than an RDBMS here?
options: 它把查询约束成主键访问，换来简单的路由和水平扩展
它自动提供任意字段过滤和多表 join
它要求所有写入走单个 leader 保证串行顺序
它通过固定 schema 降低 value 的版本管理成本
options_en: It narrows access to primary-key lookups, which makes routing and horizontal scaling simpler.
It automatically supports arbitrary field filters and multi-table joins.
It requires all writes to go through one leader for serial order.
It uses a fixed schema to reduce value-version management costs.
why: 我会选 KV store，因为题目只需要按 key 取小对象，数据分片可以直接跟 hash 走。代价是放弃 RDBMS 那套丰富查询和强事务模型。
why_en: A KV store fits because the workload is primary-key access, while the cost is giving up rich relational queries and transactions.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品要大量 join、二级索引过滤和跨实体事务，RDBMS 会更自然。
tradeoff: 主键扩展性 vs 查询表达力

termDefinitions.meaning: RDBMS 是关系数据库管理系统，擅长表、join、事务和声明式查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An RDBMS manages relational tables and is strong at joins, transactions, and declarative queries.

q: Dynamo 风格 KV store 的一致性配置何时确定？
q_en: When is consistency configuration chosen in a Dynamo-style key-value store?
text: 在这个设计里，一致性、可用性、成本和性能的取舍参数应在实例创建时配置，运行中{{不动态修改}}。
text_en: In this design, consistency, availability, cost, and performance knobs are set when the instance is created and are {{not changed dynamically}} at runtime.
why: 这样做能让路由、复制和 quorum 语义稳定。运行时随意改参数会让客户端难以判断一次读写到底承诺了什么。
why_en: Static instance-level settings keep routing, replication, and quorum semantics predictable for clients.

scenario: KV store 遇到网络分区时，业务要求购物车、会话等写入仍被接收，短时间读到旧版本可以接受。
scenario_en: During a network partition, the service must still accept cart and session writes, and short-lived stale reads are acceptable.
q: CAP 取舍应偏向哪一边？
q_en: Which side of the CAP tradeoff should this design favor?
options: CP：拒绝分区侧写入，先保证所有副本一致
AP：继续接收读写，之后用版本合并修复分歧
CA：忽略网络分区，只优化单机一致性
单 leader 串行：所有请求跨分区转到 leader
options_en: CP: reject writes on the partitioned side and preserve replica consistency first.
AP: keep accepting reads and writes, then repair divergence with version reconciliation.
CA: ignore partitions and optimize only single-site consistency.
Single leader: forward every request across the partition to the leader.
optionMeanings: CP 在分区时牺牲可用性。
AP 在分区时保住可用性。
CA 不处理分布式分区现实。
leader 串行把写入口集中起来。
optionDirectness: 适合银行账本这类宁停不乱的场景。
适合用户体验更怕写失败的场景。
只适合单机或同机房小系统讨论。
适合强顺序但网络稳定的部署。
optionScenarioImpacts: 购物车写入会在分区期间失败。
可能出现冲突版本，需要后续合并。
题目的故障模型没有被解决。
分区侧请求会超时或不可达。
why: 我会选 AP，因为题目把“能写进去”放在一致读之前。代价是系统要保存并暴露冲突版本，靠 vector clock 和客户端合并收口。
why_en: I would favor AP because accepting writes matters more than immediate consistency, but the system must later reconcile conflicting versions.
whenOtherWins: 如果写错一次就不可接受，例如资金扣款或库存扣减，CP 或强 leader 方案会更合适。
tradeoff: 写可用性 vs 立即一致性

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 指分布式系统在网络分区下无法同时提供强一致和完全可用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP says a distributed system under partition cannot simultaneously provide strong consistency and full availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: AP 系统在分区时优先响应请求，允许副本短暂不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An AP system keeps serving requests during partitions and allows temporary replica divergence.

termDefinitions.meaning: CP 系统在分区时优先一致性，可能拒绝部分请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CP system preserves consistency during partitions and may reject some requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: vector clock 用每个节点的计数器记录版本因果关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector clock records causal version history with per-node counters.

scenario: 集群会逐步加入不同容量的新机器，系统不希望某一类特殊节点成为瓶颈或升级前置条件。
scenario_en: The cluster will gradually add machines with different capacities, and the system should avoid special nodes becoming bottlenecks or upgrade gates.
q: 节点角色应如何设计？
q_en: How should node roles be designed?
options: 所有节点 peer-to-peer，对外都能协调读写
固定少数 master 节点负责所有写入
让最高配置机器永久保存全部热点 key
每次扩容都先停机重新分配全量数据
options_en: Use peer-to-peer nodes where any node can coordinate reads or writes.
Use a small fixed set of master nodes for all writes.
Keep all hot keys forever on the highest-capacity machines.
Stop the cluster and redistribute all data on every scale-out.
why: 我会让节点对等，再用 virtual nodes 按容量分摊负载。这样新机器加入不要求升级旧机器，也不会把写入口压到少数 master 上。
why_en: Peer-to-peer nodes plus capacity-weighted virtual nodes let heterogeneous machines join without creating master bottlenecks.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统规模小且强一致写顺序最重要，单 leader 或少量 master 会更容易实现。
tradeoff: 去中心化扩展 vs 集中式顺序控制

termDefinitions.meaning: peer-to-peer 表示节点角色对等，没有固定主节点承担所有协调工作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Peer-to-peer means nodes have equal roles rather than a fixed master coordinating everything.

termDefinitions.meaning: virtual node 是物理节点在 hash ring 上的多个逻辑位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A virtual node is one logical position owned by a physical node on the hash ring.

q: Dynamo 风格 `get(key)` 可能返回哪些信息？
q_en: What can a Dynamo-style get(key) return?
options: 某个 key 的一个 value
同一个 key 的多个冲突版本
用于后续 put 的版本上下文
跨 key 的 SQL join 结果
options_en: A single value for a key.
Multiple conflicting versions for the same key.
Version context to pass into a later put.
A SQL join result across keys.
why: 弱一致复制下，读请求可能看到同一 key 的多个叶子版本，所以系统要把 value 和版本 context 一起交给客户端。跨 key join 不是这个 API 的目标。
why_en: A weakly consistent KV read may return one or more versions plus context, but it is not a cross-key join API.

termDefinitions.meaning: context 是随对象返回的版本元数据，客户端在下一次写入时带回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Context is version metadata returned with an object and supplied again on a later write.

q: Dynamo 风格 KV store 如何把 key 映射到 ring？
q_en: How does a Dynamo-style KV store map keys onto the ring?
text: 系统对 key 做 hash 得到固定长度标识符；Dynamo 的经典设计使用 {{MD5}} 产生 {{128-bit}} ID，再用它定位负责节点。
text_en: The system hashes the key into a fixed-length identifier; the classic Dynamo design uses {{MD5}} to produce a {{128-bit}} ID for placement.
why: hash 后的 ID 让任意字符串 key 落到统一的地址空间里。后续 consistent hashing、replica placement 和 preference list 都围绕这个空间工作。
why_en: Hashing keys into one ID space lets consistent hashing and replica placement use the same ring abstraction.

termDefinitions.meaning: MD5 是一种产生 128-bit 摘要的 hash 算法；这里用于定位，不用于安全签名。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MD5 is a hash algorithm that produces a 128-bit digest; here it is used for placement, not security.

scenario: KV 集群用 `hash(key) % m` 分片。现在从 4 个节点变成 3 个节点，节点本地缓存了自己负责的数据。
scenario_en: A KV cluster shards with hash(key) % m. It shrinks from 4 nodes to 3, and each node locally caches its owned data.
q: 为什么取模分片扩缩容代价高？
q_en: Why is modulo sharding expensive during scale changes?
options: m 变了会让大量 key 换节点，引发数据搬迁和缓存失效
取模会让所有 key 永远落到同一个节点
取模无法用 hash 函数生成数字
取模只影响读路径，不影响数据放置
options_en: Changing m moves many keys to different nodes, causing data movement and cache misses.
Modulo always maps every key to the same node.
Modulo cannot use a hash function to produce numbers.
Modulo only affects reads and not data placement.
why: 问题不在取模算不出来，而是分母一变，大部分 key 的余数都会变。节点要搬大量数据，读请求也会打到没有缓存的新 owner。
why_en: Modulo sharding is painful because changing the divisor remaps many keys, forcing data movement and cache misses.
tradeoff: 实现简单 vs 扩缩容扰动

scenario: 你要让 KV store 支持频繁加机器和退机器，同时尽量少移动已有 key。
scenario_en: You need a KV store to add and remove machines often while moving as few existing keys as possible.
q: 为什么选择 consistent hashing？
q_en: Why choose consistent hashing?
options: 它把 hash 空间做成 ring，只让相邻区间在节点变化时移动
它要求所有节点保存完整数据副本
它让每次扩容都重新计算全量 SQL 索引
它用物理时间决定每个 key 的 owner
options_en: It models the hash space as a ring, so only neighboring ranges move when nodes change.
It requires every node to store a full copy of all data.
It rebuilds all SQL indexes on every scale-out.
It uses physical time to decide the owner for each key.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  K["hash(key)"] --> P["position on ring"]
  P --> N["first node clockwise"]
  J["new node joins"]
  J --> S["takes slice from successor"]
  S --> O["other ranges unchanged"]
why: consistent hashing 的核心收益是节点变更只影响 ring 上一段相邻 key。它不是让数据不动，而是把搬迁从近似全量降到局部区间。
why_en: Consistent hashing limits movement to neighboring ranges on the ring instead of remapping most keys.
whenOtherWins: 如果节点数固定且永不扩缩容，简单取模分片的实现成本更低。
tradeoff: 局部搬迁 vs 路由复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: consistent hashing 把 key 和节点都映射到 ring 上，key 归顺时针遇到的第一个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps keys and nodes onto a ring, and a key belongs to the first node clockwise.

q: consistent hashing 中新节点加入时谁受影响？
q_en: Who is affected when a new node joins a consistent-hashing ring?
text: 新节点加入 ring 时，它通常只从顺时针方向的{{后继节点}}接管一段 key；其他节点的 key 区间保持不变。
text_en: When a node joins the ring, it usually takes a key slice from its clockwise {{successor}}, while other nodes keep their ranges.
why: 这就是一致哈希降低扩缩容扰动的地方。新节点和 successor 做数据交接，不需要全体节点一起重排。
why_en: A joining node only exchanges data with its successor, which avoids a cluster-wide reshuffle.

scenario: consistent hashing ring 上有些节点拥有很长的 hash 弧段，导致请求和数据集中到少数机器。
scenario_en: Some nodes on a consistent-hashing ring own long arcs, so requests and data concentrate on a few machines.
q: 如何缓解 ring 上的热点？
q_en: How can you reduce hotspots on the ring?
options: 给每台物理机放多个 virtual nodes，让区间交错分布
把所有热点 key 固定迁到第一台机器
取消 hash，改成客户端随机选节点
每次热点出现就全量重建 ring
options_en: Place multiple virtual nodes per physical machine so ranges interleave.
Move every hot key permanently to the first machine.
Remove hashing and let clients pick random nodes.
Rebuild the entire ring whenever a hotspot appears.
why: virtual nodes 把一台物理机拆成多个 ring 位置，长弧段风险会被摊薄。某台机器故障时，它的负载也会散到多个邻居，而不是压给一个 successor。
why_en: Virtual nodes interleave each physical machine across the ring, smoothing load and spreading failover pressure.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有几台机器和很小数据量，单位置 ring 可能够用，省掉 vnode 管理成本。
tradeoff: 负载均衡 vs 元数据数量

termDefinitions.meaning: hotspot 是某个节点或 key range 承担远高于平均的请求或数据压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hotspot is a node or key range carrying much more traffic or data than average.

scenario: KV 集群里既有老机器也有新机器，新机器 CPU、磁盘和网络容量更高。
scenario_en: The KV cluster has both old and new machines, and the new machines have more CPU, disk, and network capacity.
q: virtual nodes 如何表达机器容量差异？
q_en: How can virtual nodes represent capacity differences?
options: 给高容量机器分配更多 vnode，让它拥有更多 key range
让所有机器 vnode 数严格相同，避免任何倾斜
只让低容量机器接收写入，高容量机器空闲
把容量信息写进 value，由客户端自行选择节点
options_en: Assign more vnodes to higher-capacity machines so they own more key ranges.
Give every machine exactly the same vnode count to avoid any skew.
Send writes only to low-capacity machines and leave high-capacity machines idle.
Put capacity metadata in values and make clients choose nodes themselves.
why: vnode 数量可以当作权重，高配机器拿更多区间，也就承担更多读写和存储。这样不用要求所有节点硬件同质。
why_en: The vnode count acts as a weight, so larger machines can own more ranges without requiring homogeneous hardware.
whenOtherWins: 如果运维上强制所有机器规格一致，等量 vnode 更简单。
tradeoff: 容量利用率 vs ring 元数据管理

scenario: KV store 要在节点故障和网络分区时继续接收写入，业务能接受短暂版本分歧。
scenario_en: The KV store must continue accepting writes during node failures and partitions, and the business accepts temporary version divergence.
q: 复制模型应选 primary-secondary 还是 peer-to-peer？
q_en: Should replication be primary-secondary or peer-to-peer?
options: primary-secondary：一个 primary 负责写，副本异步跟随
peer-to-peer：任意节点可协调读写，再复制到 preference list
全量复制：每次写同步到集群所有节点
无复制：每个 key 只保存在一个节点上
options_en: Primary-secondary: one primary handles writes and replicas follow asynchronously.
Peer-to-peer: any node can coordinate reads and writes, then replicate to the preference list.
Full replication: synchronously write every update to every node in the cluster.
No replication: keep each key on exactly one node.
optionMeanings: 写入口集中在 primary。
节点角色对等，按 key 选 coordinator。
所有节点都保存每个 key。
没有副本冗余。
optionDirectness: 适合强主写顺序和较小规模。
适合 AP 和无特殊节点要求。
适合极小配置数据。
适合可从源系统重建的缓存。
optionScenarioImpacts: primary 故障前写入会卡住。
分区侧仍能写，但会产生冲突版本。
写放大和存储成本过高。
节点丢失就可能丢数据。
why: 我会选 peer-to-peer，因为题目要求故障时继续写，不能让 primary 成为写入单点。代价是系统要接受副本短暂分歧，并用版本与 quorum 收敛。
why_en: Peer-to-peer replication fits because writes must survive failures, but it requires versioning and quorum logic to converge later.
whenOtherWins: 如果强顺序写和简单运维比可用性更重要，primary-secondary 会更容易讲清楚。
tradeoff: 写可用性 vs 复制冲突复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: SPOF 是单点故障，一个组件失效会让整条能力不可用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A SPOF is a single component whose failure can take down a whole capability.

q: preference list 如何避免副本落到同一物理机？
q_en: How does a preference list avoid placing replicas on the same physical machine?
text: 复制因子为 n 时，coordinator 选择 ring 上后续节点作为副本；构造 preference list 时要跳过已经出现过的{{同一物理节点}}的 vnode。
text_en: With replication factor n, the coordinator picks successors on the ring; the preference list skips vnodes that belong to an already selected {{physical node}}.
why: vnode 是逻辑位置，不跳过同一物理机就会把多个副本放在同一故障域。复制的目标是抗机器故障，不只是凑够 ring 位置。
why_en: Skipping vnodes on the same physical node keeps replicas in separate failure domains.

termDefinitions.meaning: preference list 是某个 key 按 ring 顺序选出的副本节点列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A preference list is the ordered set of replica nodes selected for a key on the ring.

scenario: 两个数据中心之间断网，分区两侧都有用户继续更新同一个购物车 key。
scenario_en: Two data centers are partitioned, and users on both sides keep updating the same cart key.
q: AP KV store 会产生什么后果？
q_en: What consequence should an AP KV store expect?
options: 两侧继续写入，恢复后可能出现多个需要合并的版本
所有写入自动按真实发生时间排成唯一顺序
分区期间所有节点立即删除该 key
系统不需要记录任何版本元数据
options_en: Both sides keep writing, and after repair there may be multiple versions to reconcile.
All writes are automatically ordered by their true real-world time.
Every node immediately deletes the key during the partition.
The system no longer needs any version metadata.
why: AP 的承诺是分区时继续服务，不是自动知道哪次写“最后”。恢复后要把并发分支交给冲突解决流程。
why_en: AP keeps serving during partitions, so it must later reconcile concurrent branches instead of assuming a true last write.
tradeoff: 分区可用性 vs 冲突解决成本

scenario: 同一个 key 在网络分区期间被不同节点更新，机器物理时钟可能漂移，系统要判断版本是先后关系还是并发冲突。
scenario_en: The same key is updated on different nodes during a partition, physical clocks may drift, and the system must tell ancestry from conflict.
q: 版本元数据应选什么？
q_en: What version metadata should the system use?
options: 物理 timestamp：谁时间大谁赢
vector clock：记录各节点 counter 来比较因果
随机 UUID：冲突时按字符串排序
自增全局序列：每个节点本地独立加一
options_en: Physical timestamp: the larger clock value wins.
Vector clock: track per-node counters to compare causality.
Random UUID: sort strings to resolve conflicts.
Global sequence: each node independently increments a local counter.
optionMeanings: 依赖机器墙钟。
记录每个写入节点的版本计数。
给版本一个随机标识。
每个节点自己发号。
optionDirectness: 适合时钟强同步且容忍误判。
适合分区后判断因果和并发。
适合唯一命名，不适合因果判断。
适合单节点或有中心发号器。
optionScenarioImpacts: clock skew 会误删较新的逻辑更新。
系统能返回冲突分支给客户端。
只能区分对象，不能比较历史。
分区下会产生重复或乱序。
why: 我会用 vector clock，因为它比较的是“这个版本是否包含那个版本的历史”，而不是相信机器时间。代价是元数据会随参与写入的节点变多而增长。
why_en: Vector clocks fit because they compare causal history rather than trusting skewed physical clocks.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务只要粗略 last-write-wins 且时钟误差可接受，物理 timestamp 更便宜。
tradeoff: 因果准确性 vs 元数据大小

termDefinitions.meaning: clock skew 是不同机器时钟读数不一致造成的时间偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Clock skew is the difference between time readings on different machines.

q: 为什么 `put` 要带上 `get` 返回的 context？
q_en: Why should put include the context returned by get?
text: `get(key)` 返回 value 和版本 context；后续 `put(key, {{context}}, value)` 带回它，系统才能把新写入接到正确的版本历史上。
text_en: `get(key)` returns the value and version context; a later `put(key, {{context}}, value)` supplies it so the system can attach the write to the right version history.
why: context 相当于客户端看到的父版本。没有它，系统只知道来了一个新 value，却不知道它是在覆盖旧版本还是在合并冲突。
why_en: The context identifies the parent version the client observed, so the system can distinguish overwrite from conflict merge.
codeSample:
get(cart:42) -> { value, context: "vc:A=2,B=1" }
put(cart:42, context="vc:A=2,B=1", value=mergedCart)

scenario: 在 Dynamo 风格 KV store 中，vector clock 是每个版本携带的节点 counter 列表，用来比较版本历史。
scenario_en: In a Dynamo-style KV store, a vector clock is the node-counter list attached to each version to compare version history.
q: 比较两个 vector clocks 时能判断哪些关系？
q_en: What relationships can vector-clock comparison reveal?
options: 一个版本包含另一个版本的因果历史
两个版本互不包含，属于并发冲突
两个版本完全相同
哪个机房的物理时钟更准
options_en: One version causally includes the other version's history.
Neither version includes the other, so they are concurrent conflicts.
The two versions are identical.
Which data center has the more accurate physical clock.
why: vector clock 比的是每个节点 counter 的包含关系。它能判断祖先、相同和并发，但不测量墙钟准确度。
why_en: Vector-clock comparison checks counter inclusion, so it can detect ancestry, equality, and concurrency, not clock accuracy.

termDefinitions.meaning: vector clock 是每个版本携带的节点计数器列表，用来比较版本之间的因果包含关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector clock is a list of per-node counters attached to a version to compare causal inclusion.

termDefinitions.meaning: counter 是某个节点在版本历史中递增的计数值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A counter is the value a node increments in a version history.

scenario: 同一个 key 在网络分区期间分叉；vector clock 用节点 counter 记录每个版本来自哪条历史。
scenario_en: The same key diverges during a network partition; vector clocks use node counters to record each version's history.
q: vector clock 冲突到合并的顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the order from vector-clock conflict to merge?
steps: 客户端读取到两个 leaf versions，并看到它们互不包含
分区两侧分别写出 [A:2,B:1] 和 [A:2,C:1]
客户端按业务规则合并 value
A 节点先写出父版本 [A:2]
协调节点写入合并结果，并把自己的 counter 加一
why: 完整链条是先有共同父版本，再在分区里分叉，读时暴露 leaf versions，最后由业务合并并写回新版本。代价是客户端要懂对象语义。
why_en: The chain is parent, divergent writes, exposed leaf versions, application merge, and a new version written back by the coordinator.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A
  participant B
  participant C
  participant Client
  A->>A: E2 [A:2]
  B->>B: E3 [A:2,B:1]
  C->>C: E4 [A:2,C:1]
  Client->>A: get(key)
  A-->>Client: E3 + E4
  Client->>A: put(merged, context)
  A->>A: E5 [A:3,B:1,C:1]

termDefinitions.meaning: vector clock 是每个版本携带的节点计数器列表，用来判断版本是否同源或冲突。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector clock is a per-node counter list attached to a version to detect ancestry or conflict.

termDefinitions.meaning: leaf version 是当前没有被更新版本覆盖的分支末端版本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A leaf version is a branch-tip version that has not been superseded by a newer version.

termDefinitions.meaning: counter 是节点在写入新版本时递增的本地版本号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A counter is the local version number a node increments when it writes a new version.

scenario: 某个热点 key 在故障和分区期间被很多非首选节点写入，vector clock 已经有十几个 `(node,counter)` 条目。
scenario_en: A hot key is written by many non-preferred nodes during failures and partitions, and its vector clock now has many node-counter entries.
q: 截断 vector clock 的风险是什么？
q_en: What is the risk of truncating a vector clock?
options: 可能丢掉因果历史，让系统更难准确判断祖先和冲突
会让 value 的二进制内容自动损坏
会让所有副本立即变成强一致
会阻止任何节点继续写入该 key
options_en: It may drop causal history, making ancestry and conflict checks less accurate.
It automatically corrupts the binary value.
It immediately makes all replicas strongly consistent.
It prevents any node from writing that key again.
why: 截断是控制元数据大小的工程折中，不是免费优化。删掉老条目后，某些版本关系可能从“可判断”变成“只能当冲突处理”。
why_en: Truncation controls metadata size, but it can discard causal evidence and force conservative conflict handling.
tradeoff: 元数据上限 vs 因果判断精度

scenario: 客户端要访问 KV store。你可以让普通负载均衡器随便转发，也可以把 ring 路由逻辑放进客户端库。
scenario_en: Clients access the KV store through either a generic load balancer or a client library that understands ring placement.
q: partition-aware client library 的收益是什么？
q_en: What is the benefit of a partition-aware client library?
options: 客户端能直接找 coordinator，少一次中转
客户端不再需要处理任何错误
所有 value 都自动变成强一致
它完全取消服务器端复制
options_en: The client can contact the coordinator directly and avoid an extra hop.
The client never has to handle any error.
All values automatically become strongly consistent.
It removes server-side replication entirely.
why: 懂分区的客户端能自己算 key 的 coordinator，延迟少一个 LB 转发。代价是客户端要跟随 ring 和成员变更升级。
why_en: A partition-aware client can route directly to the coordinator, saving a hop at the cost of client-side placement complexity.
tradeoff: 更低延迟 vs 客户端复杂度

scenario: 一个 key 有 n=3 个副本。你希望一次读和最近一次成功写至少在一个副本上相交。
scenario_en: A key has n=3 replicas. You want every read quorum to overlap with the latest successful write quorum on at least one replica.
q: r 和 w 应满足什么条件？
q_en: What condition should r and w satisfy?
options: r + w > n
r + w = n
r = 1 且 w = 1
r 和 w 都必须等于 0
options_en: r + w > n.
r + w = n.
r = 1 and w = 1.
Both r and w must be zero.
why: r+w>n 逼迫读集合和写集合至少重叠一个副本，读才有机会看到最新写。n=3 时 r=2,w=2 可行，r=2,w=1 不够。
why_en: The rule r + w > n forces read and write quorums to overlap on at least one replica.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务明确接受更弱读一致性，可以放宽重叠要求来换更高可用性和更低延迟。
tradeoff: 读到新值概率 vs quorum 延迟和可用性

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是一次读或写必须等到的最少副本响应数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum number of replica responses required for a read or write to succeed.

scenario: KV store 使用 n=3。某业务读多写少，希望读请求尽量快，能接受写路径等更多副本确认。
scenario_en: The KV store uses n=3. A read-heavy service wants fast reads and can accept waiting for more replicas on writes.
q: 应如何调 r 和 w？
q_en: How should r and w be tuned?
why: r=1 让读只等最快副本，w=3 把成本转到写路径，并且 r+w>n 仍成立。读延迟由等到的最慢 r 个响应决定，r 越大读越慢。
why_en: Use r=1 and w=3 to make reads wait for one replica while preserving quorum overlap by paying more on writes.
tradeoff: 读延迟 vs 写延迟

q: 一次 `put` 的 quorum 写入顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the order of a quorum write for put?
steps: coordinator 在本地生成新 vector clock 并写本地副本
客户端把 key、context 和 value 发给 coordinator
coordinator 把写入转发给 preference list 里的其他副本
至少 w 个副本确认后，coordinator 向客户端返回成功
未及时确认的副本后续通过修复流程补齐
why: coordinator 自己算一个确认，所以还要等 w-1 个其他副本。代价是未同步副本会短暂落后，后续要靠 read repair、handoff 或 anti-entropy 修复。
why_en: A put succeeds after the coordinator and enough replicas acknowledge it, while lagging replicas are repaired later.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant Q as Coordinator
  participant R1 as Replica1
  participant R2 as Replica2
  C->>Q: put(key, context, value)
  Q->>Q: write local + new vector clock
  Q->>R1: replicate
  Q->>R2: replicate
  R1-->>Q: ack
  Q-->>C: success when w acks

q: 一次 `get` 发现冲突版本后如何收口？
q_en: How does a get converge after finding conflicting versions?
steps: 客户端按业务规则把多个 value 合成一个新 value
coordinator 查询 top n 个可达副本
系统比较 vector clocks，发现互不包含的版本
coordinator 等到 r 个响应后返回 leaf versions 和 context
客户端带合并后的 value 和 context 再次 put
why: 读路径先凑够 r 个响应，再用版本元数据判断是否有分叉。系统不懂购物车或偏好设置的业务语义时，会把合并责任交给客户端。
why_en: The read path gathers r responses, detects divergent leaf versions, and lets the client merge when application semantics are needed.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C[client get] --> Q[coordinator]
  Q --> R[query n replicas]
  R --> W[wait for r]
  W --> V{versions related?}
  V -- yes --> One[return latest]
  V -- no --> Many[return versions + context]
  Many --> Merge[client merges]
  Merge --> Put[put merged value]

scenario: 某个 key 的首选副本里有节点临时宕机。业务仍要求写入成功，等节点恢复后再补数据。
scenario_en: One preferred replica for a key is temporarily down. The business still wants writes to succeed and repair when the node returns.
q: 应该用 strict quorum 还是 sloppy quorum？
q_en: Should the system use strict quorum or sloppy quorum?
options: strict quorum：只允许首选 n 个 owner 响应
sloppy quorum：健康后继节点临时代收
停止写入：等所有首选副本恢复
删除该 key：避免不一致
options_en: Strict quorum: only the preferred n owners may respond.
Sloppy quorum: use healthy successor nodes as temporary holders.
Stop writes until all preferred replicas recover.
Delete the key to avoid inconsistency.
why: 我会用 sloppy quorum，因为题目把临时故障下的写可用性放在第一位。代价是临时代收节点要保存 hint，恢复后把数据交还原 owner。
why_en: Sloppy quorum keeps writes available by using healthy fallback nodes, but it needs hinted handoff to return data later.
whenOtherWins: 如果合规要求副本必须只落在指定 owner 上，strict quorum 更可控但可用性更低。
tradeoff: 临时可用性 vs 副本归属纯度

termDefinitions.meaning: sloppy quorum 使用前 n 个健康节点响应，而不只限于原始 owner。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sloppy quorum uses the first healthy nodes instead of only the original owners.

termDefinitions.meaning: hinted handoff 是临时节点带着归属提示保存数据，owner 恢复后再交还。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hinted handoff stores data on a temporary node with a hint and hands it back when the owner recovers.

q: hinted handoff 的恢复链路是什么？
q_en: What is the recovery chain for hinted handoff?
steps: A 恢复后，D 把暂存数据转发给 A
写入到来时，原 owner A 临时不可达
D 删除自己的临时副本
coordinator 选择后续健康节点 D 临时代收
D 保存 value，并记录 hint：这份数据属于 A
why: 完整链条是 owner 不可达、健康节点代收、hint 记录归属、owner 恢复后交还、临时副本清理。代价是恢复前读到哪个副本会影响新旧程度。
why_en: Hinted handoff writes to a temporary healthy node, records the real owner, hands data back on recovery, and then deletes the temporary copy.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Q as Coordinator
  participant A as Owner A down
  participant D as Healthy D
  Q->>A: write
  A--xQ: unavailable
  Q->>D: store with hint owner=A
  A-->>D: recovers
  D->>A: hand off data
  D->>D: delete temporary copy

q: 为什么临时故障处理不足以覆盖机房灾难？
q_en: Why is temporary-failure handling not enough for data-center disasters?
text: hinted handoff 能处理短暂节点故障；如果整座机房断电或灾难失效，需要把副本跨{{独立数据中心}}放置。
text_en: Hinted handoff handles short node outages; if a whole data center fails, replicas must be placed across {{independent data centers}}.
why: 节点级临时代收解决的是局部不可达。机房级故障会同时打掉同一故障域里的多个副本，所以副本放置要跨故障域。
why_en: Node-level handoff handles local outages, while data-center failure requires replicas in separate failure domains.

scenario: 一个副本长时间离线后回归，系统要找出它和健康副本之间哪些 key range 不一致，但不能全量扫描和传输全部数据。
scenario_en: A replica returns after a long outage, and the system must find inconsistent key ranges without scanning and transferring the full dataset.
q: 应该用什么反熵机制？
q_en: What anti-entropy mechanism should be used?
options: Merkle tree：先比 root hash，再递归定位差异范围
随机抽样：只查几个 key，没发现就认为一致
全量复制：每次恢复都传完整数据集
物理 timestamp：只保留时间戳最大的副本
options_en: Merkle tree: compare root hashes, then recurse to locate differing ranges.
Random sampling: check a few keys and assume consistency if none differ.
Full copy: transfer the entire dataset on every recovery.
Physical timestamp: keep only the replica with the largest clock.
why: Merkle tree 让两个副本先比摘要，只有摘要不同的子树才继续下钻。代价是 key range 变化时树要重算，尤其节点加入或离开后。
why_en: Merkle trees narrow repair to differing ranges by comparing hashes, but range changes require rebuilding tree state.
whenOtherWins: 如果数据集很小，全量复制可能比维护 hash tree 更省工程成本。
tradeoff: 修复带宽 vs 树维护成本

termDefinitions.meaning: Merkle tree 是 hash tree，叶子是数据 hash，父节点是子 hash 的摘要。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Merkle tree is a hash tree whose leaves hash data and whose parents hash child hashes.

termDefinitions.meaning: anti-entropy 是副本之间后台比较并修复不一致数据的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Anti-entropy is background comparison and repair between replicas.

q: Merkle tree 如何定位副本差异？
q_en: How does a Merkle tree locate replica differences?
steps: 如果 root 不同，只递归比较不同分支的 child hash
两个副本先交换某个 key range 的 root hash
定位到不同叶子或小范围后，只同步这些 key
如果 root 相同，认为该范围一致
节点范围变化时，相关 tree 需要重新计算
why: 正常路径是先用 root hash 快速排除一致范围，异常时沿不同分支下钻，最后只传不一致 key。成本收尾是 ring 变化会让 range 和 tree 失效。
why_en: Merkle repair compares roots first, drills only into differing branches, transfers only bad keys, and pays rebuild cost when ranges change.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[exchange root hash] --> B{same?}
  B -- yes --> C[range identical]
  B -- no --> D[compare child hashes]
  D --> E[find differing leaves]
  E --> F[sync only those keys]
  G[node joins/leaves] --> H[recompute affected trees]

scenario: KV 集群里节点会短暂抖动或网络超时。你不希望每次短故障都触发 ring 重平衡和大规模数据迁移。
scenario_en: Nodes in the KV cluster can briefly flap or time out, and you do not want every short outage to trigger ring rebalancing and large data movement.
q: 故障检测应如何处理短暂离线？
q_en: How should failure detection treat short outages?
options: 先标疑似故障，持续失败才改 membership
第一次心跳失败就永久移出 ring 并搬迁
每次失败都立即复制全量数据到所有节点
完全不记录节点状态，靠客户端猜测
options_en: Mark it as suspect first, and change membership only after sustained failure.
Remove it from the ring permanently after the first missed heartbeat and move data.
Copy the full dataset to every node after every failure.
Do not record node state, and make clients guess.
why: 我会把短故障和 membership 变更分开。短抖动用 sloppy quorum、handoff 和重试吸收，持续失败或计划下线才调整 ring。
why_en: Short outages should be absorbed without membership changes, while sustained failures or planned changes update the ring.
whenOtherWins: 如果节点已经确定永久退役，及时改 membership 才能释放责任区间。
tradeoff: 避免抖动迁移 vs 故障收敛速度

scenario: KV store 没有中心 membership 服务。每个节点本地持久化成员变更历史，需要低带宽地传播到全体节点。
scenario_en: The KV store has no central membership service. Each node persists membership history locally and needs to spread it with low bandwidth.
q: 应如何传播 membership？
q_en: How should membership be propagated?
options: gossip：节点随机互相同步 membership history
单中心表：所有节点每毫秒同步读一个主库
客户端广播：每个客户端维护全量节点状态
关闭持久化：重启后重新猜测集群成员
options_en: Gossip: nodes randomly exchange membership history with peers.
Single central table: every node polls one primary database every millisecond.
Client broadcast: every client maintains the full node state.
Disable persistence and guess membership again after restart.
why: gossip 让 membership 视图最终一致，不需要单点协调者。代价是传播有延迟，所以不能把它当作强一致配置总线。
why_en: Gossip spreads membership without a coordinator, but the view is eventually consistent rather than instant.
whenOtherWins: 如果集群很小且已有可靠控制平面，中心 membership 服务更容易审计。
tradeoff: 去中心化传播 vs 收敛延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: gossip 是节点随机选 peer 交换状态，经过多轮让全体逐步收敛的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Gossip is a protocol where nodes randomly exchange state with peers until the cluster converges.

q: gossip 中 token set 表示什么？
q_en: What does a token set represent in gossip membership?
text: 在 consistent hashing 集群里，token set 表示节点在 hash 空间中拥有的{{virtual nodes}}或 token 位置。
text_en: In a consistent-hashing cluster, a token set represents the {{virtual nodes}} or token positions owned by a node in the hash space.
why: membership 不只是知道“有这台机器”，还要知道它负责哪些 ring 位置。gossip 同步这些历史后，节点才能对 key placement 达成最终一致。
why_en: Membership includes both machines and their ring positions, so gossip must converge on token ownership.

scenario: 同一台物理机的多个 vnode 被当成独立成员分别加入 ring，并各自传播 membership 更新。
scenario_en: Multiple vnodes from the same physical machine join the ring as if they were independent members and spread membership updates separately.
q: 这种做法有什么风险？
q_en: What risk does this create?
options: 可能造成逻辑分区，让不同节点学到不一致的更新集合
会让所有 key 自动均匀到每个机房
会消除物理机故障域问题
会让 vector clock 不再需要 counter
options_en: It can create logical partitioning where nodes learn inconsistent update sets.
It automatically balances all keys across every data center.
It removes physical-machine failure-domain risk.
It makes vector clocks no longer need counters.
optionMeanings: 同机 vnode 被当成独立成员传播。
把 membership 问题误当负载均衡问题。
误以为逻辑节点能消除物理故障域。
把 gossip 风险和版本元数据混在一起。
optionDirectness: 适合检查 vnode 与物理节点绑定是否正确。
适合讨论跨机房 placement，不适合本题。
适合反驳单机多 vnode 的误解。
适合 vector clock 卡，不适合 membership 卡。
optionScenarioImpacts: 不同节点可能收敛到不同成员历史。
无法解释更新集合不一致。
同一物理机故障仍会打掉多个 vnode。
counter 是否存在不解决 gossip 分裂。
why: vnode 是逻辑位置，但故障和 membership 语义仍要绑回物理节点。把同机 vnode 当独立成员传播，可能让集群状态分裂。
why_en: Vnodes are logical positions, but membership and failure semantics must still be tied to physical nodes.
tradeoff: vnode 细粒度路由 vs 物理节点成员语义

termDefinitions.meaning: vnode 是 physical node 在 hash ring 上拥有的一个逻辑位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vnode is one logical hash-ring position owned by a physical node.

termDefinitions.meaning: membership 是集群当前有哪些物理节点以及它们负责哪些 token 的成员视图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Membership is the cluster view of which physical nodes exist and which tokens they own.

termDefinitions.meaning: gossip 是节点随机互相交换状态，让成员信息逐步收敛的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Gossip is a protocol where nodes randomly exchange state until membership converges.

termDefinitions.meaning: vector clock 是版本因果元数据；本题中它是干扰项，不负责传播 membership。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector clock is causal version metadata; here it is a distractor and does not propagate membership.

termDefinitions.meaning: counter 是 vector clock 中某个节点的递增计数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A counter is the per-node incrementing value inside a vector clock.

scenario: 一个分布式系统每天产生海量帖子、支付或跟踪事件，多个分片和服务实例会并行写数据库主键。
scenario_en: A distributed system creates massive post, payment, or tracing events daily, and many shards and service instances write primary keys in parallel.
q: 为什么不能只靠单机 auto-increment？
q_en: Why not rely on a single-machine auto-increment column?
options: 多节点并行生成时会争用中心点或产生重复 ID
auto-increment 不能生成任何数字
数据库主键不需要唯一
分布式系统只能使用字符串主键
options_en: Parallel nodes either contend on a central point or risk duplicate IDs.
Auto-increment cannot generate numbers at all.
Database primary keys do not need to be unique.
Distributed systems can only use string primary keys.
why: 单机自增在一个数据库里很好用，但跨分片、跨服务时会变成中心瓶颈。分布式 sequencer 要在唯一性、吞吐和可用性之间取舍。
why_en: Single-node auto-increment works locally, but distributed ID generation must handle uniqueness, throughput, and availability across nodes.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有写入天然只进一个小型数据库，auto-increment 是最简单方案。
tradeoff: 本地简单性 vs 分布式唯一性

scenario: 事件 ID 会用于调试一次请求穿过上百个微服务的路径，也会用于按创建时间做范围扫描。
scenario_en: Event IDs are used to trace a request across many microservices and to range-scan records by creation time.
q: time-sortable ID 带来什么收益？
q_en: What benefit does a time-sortable ID provide?
options: 仅按 ID 排序就能近似按创建时间排序
它保证所有跨地域事件都有严格因果顺序
它让数据库不再需要任何索引
它自动隐藏所有业务指标
options_en: Sorting by ID also roughly sorts by creation time.
It guarantees strict causal order for all cross-region events.
It removes the need for every database index.
It automatically hides all business metrics.
why: time-sortable ID 把时间信息编码进主键，调试和范围扫描不用再额外查 timestamp 列。它通常只给时间顺序，不等于免费获得严格全局因果。
why_en: A time-sortable ID embeds time into the key, helping scans and tracing without guaranteeing strict global causality.
tradeoff: 排序便利 vs 暴露时间信息

q: 64-bit numeric ID 的量级够不够？
q_en: Is a 64-bit numeric ID space large enough?
text: 64-bit ID 空间约为 {{2^64 ≈ 1.8×10^19}}；即使一年发 365 billion 个 ID，也能支撑约 {{50 million}} 年量级。
text_en: A 64-bit ID space is about {{2^64 ≈ 1.8×10^19}}; even at 365 billion IDs per year, it lasts on the order of {{50 million}} years.
why: 这里的数字用于判断容量上限不是主要瓶颈；真正难的是分布式唯一性、可用性和顺序语义。64-bit numeric 还让索引和存储比 128-bit 随机字符串更紧凑。
why_en: The 64-bit space is huge enough that the harder problems are distributed uniqueness, availability, and ordering semantics.

termDefinitions.meaning: 64-bit 表示 ID 用 64 个二进制位编码，最多有 2^64 种组合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 64-bit means the ID is encoded with 64 binary bits, giving up to 2^64 combinations.

scenario: 服务需要无需协调地在每台机器本地生成 ID，但下游明确要求 64-bit numeric，并且希望按 ID 插入索引时更紧凑。
scenario_en: A service wants local ID generation without coordination, but downstream requires 64-bit numeric IDs and compact index inserts.
q: UUID v4 为什么不满足这个需求？
q_en: Why does UUID v4 not satisfy this requirement?
options: 它是 128-bit 随机 ID，非 64-bit 且不单调
它必须访问中心数据库才能生成每个 ID
它只能在单机上保证唯一，跨机一定重复
它会让所有事件严格按因果排序并保持 64-bit
options_en: It is a 128-bit random ID, not 64-bit and not monotonic.
It must call a central database for every generated ID.
It is unique only on one machine and always duplicates across machines.
It strictly orders every event by causality while staying 64-bit.
why: UUID 的优势是去中心化和碰撞概率极低，但它不满足 64-bit numeric，也不提供单调时间顺序。这个题的硬约束把它排除了。
why_en: UUIDs are great for decentralized generation, but they miss the 64-bit numeric and monotonic-order requirements.
tradeoff: 无需协调 vs 紧凑可排序 ID

termDefinitions.meaning: UUID 是通用唯一标识符，常见 v4 版本主要依赖随机数降低碰撞概率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UUID is a Universally Unique Identifier; version 4 mainly relies on randomness to make collisions unlikely.

scenario: 三个 ID 服务器用步长 m=3 发号：A 发 1,4,7，B 发 2,5,8，C 发 3,6,9。现在 B 失败，系统想改成 m=2。
scenario_en: Three ID servers issue numbers with step m=3: A emits 1,4,7, B emits 2,5,8, and C emits 3,6,9. B fails and the system wants m=2.
q: 为什么动态改 m 有重复风险？
q_en: Why can changing m dynamically create duplicates?
options: 剩余服务器的新序列可能踩到其他服务器已经发过的数字
步长越小，ID 空间会从 64-bit 变成 32-bit
失败服务器会自动回滚所有已发 ID
数据库自增列不允许奇数
options_en: The new sequences on remaining servers can hit numbers another server already issued.
A smaller step changes the ID space from 64-bit to 32-bit.
The failed server automatically rolls back every issued ID.
Database auto-increment columns cannot use odd numbers.
why: 发号规则一旦改步长，旧规则发出的数字还留在系统里。A 从 7 按 m=2 走到 9 时，C 可能已经发过 9。
why_en: Changing the step can make new sequences collide with IDs already emitted under the old step.
tradeoff: 中心自增简单性 vs 扩缩容安全性

scenario: 系统每天至少发 10 亿个 64-bit numeric ID，应用服务器很多；允许序列有空洞，但不允许重复。
scenario_en: The system issues at least one billion 64-bit numeric IDs per day across many app servers; gaps are acceptable but duplicates are not.
q: 为什么 range handler 是合适方案？
q_en: Why is a range handler a good fit?
options: 中心服务按段分配 ID range，应用服务器在本地递增消耗
每个应用服务器从 1 开始独立递增
用 UUID v4，忽略 64-bit numeric 要求
每次发 ID 都同步写全局单行计数器
options_en: A central service leases ID ranges, and app servers increment locally inside each range.
Every app server independently starts counting from 1.
Use UUID v4 and ignore the 64-bit numeric requirement.
Synchronously update one global counter row for every ID.
why: range handler 把中心协调从“每个 ID 一次”降到“每段一次”，所以吞吐主要在应用本地递增。代价是服务器宕机会浪费未用 range，序列出现空洞。
why_en: A range handler amortizes coordination per range instead of per ID, trading perfect gaplessness for scalable local issuance.
whenOtherWins: 如果绝对不能有空洞，就需要更强的持久化计数器或事务发号，但吞吐会低很多。
tradeoff: 高吞吐本地发号 vs 序列空洞

termDefinitions.meaning: range handler 是负责租出一段可用 ID 范围的中心微服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A range handler is a central service that leases blocks of available IDs to application servers.

q: range handler 发号链路是什么？
q_en: What is the ID issuance flow with a range handler?
steps: 应用服务器在本地从 start 递增到 end
range handler 在复制存储中把该 range 标记为 taken
应用服务器耗尽 range 后再请求下一段
应用服务器向 range handler 申请一段 ID
range handler 返回 start/end
why: 中心服务只负责租段和持久化状态，应用服务器负责段内快速发号。如果应用服务器死掉，未发完的段通常丢弃，避免重复回收。
why_en: The handler leases and persists ranges, while app servers issue locally and discard unused IDs on failure to avoid duplicates.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant App
  participant RH as Range Handler
  participant S as Replicated Store
  App->>RH: request range
  RH->>S: mark range taken
  S-->>RH: committed
  RH-->>App: start/end
  App->>App: increment locally
  App->>RH: request next when exhausted

q: range handler 自身故障时如何恢复？
q_en: How can the range handler recover from its own failure?
text: range handler 要把 range 状态写入{{replicated storage}}；主 handler 故障时，failover server 从 checkpoint 恢复已分配区间。
text_en: The range handler stores range state in {{replicated storage}}; if the primary handler fails, a failover server recovers allocated ranges from a checkpoint.
why: 发号服务不能只把已租 range 放在内存里，否则重启后可能重复分配。复制存储和 checkpoint 让新 handler 接着同一份事实工作。
why_en: Persisted replicated state prevents a restarted handler from leasing ranges that were already handed out.

termDefinitions.meaning: checkpoint 是可恢复的持久化状态快照，用来让备用服务接管。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint is a durable state snapshot that a standby service can recover from.

scenario: 评论 A 先发生，回复 B 依赖 A；同时，两个用户在不同帖子下各发一条评论，彼此没有依赖。
scenario_en: Comment A happens first and reply B depends on it, while two users commenting on different posts have no dependency between them.
q: causal order 与 total time order 的区别是什么？
q_en: How does causal order differ from total time order?
options: 因果顺序只约束有依赖的事件，并发事件不必强行排序
因果顺序要求所有事件按同一物理时钟严格排序
因果顺序只适用于单机自增 ID
因果顺序等价于随机 UUID 的字典序
options_en: Causal order constrains dependent events, while concurrent events need not be forced into one order.
Causal order requires all events to be strictly sorted by one physical clock.
Causal order applies only to single-machine auto-increment IDs.
Causal order is the same as lexicographic order of random UUIDs.
why: 因果关注的是 happened-before：回复必须在被回复评论之后。没有依赖的并发事件，可以没有业务意义上的先后。
why_en: Causal order preserves happened-before relationships, while independent concurrent events do not need a meaningful global order.
tradeoff: 必要顺序约束 vs 严格全局排序成本

scenario: 你想用机器物理时间决定跨节点事件顺序，但节点时钟会漂移，NTP 调整也可能让本地时间回拨。
scenario_en: You want to order cross-node events by physical machine time, but clocks drift and NTP adjustments can move local time backward.
q: 物理时钟方案的主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of a physical-clock-based scheme?
options: 可能生成未来时间或重复时间，破坏唯一性和因果判断
它无法表达任何毫秒数
它会自动提供完整 vector clock
它让所有数据库写入变成只读
options_en: It can produce future or repeated timestamps, breaking uniqueness and causal reasoning.
It cannot represent milliseconds at all.
It automatically provides a full vector clock.
It turns all database writes into reads.
optionMeanings: 时钟漂移或回拨让 timestamp 不可信。
误以为 timestamp 不能数值化。
把物理时钟误当因果元数据。
把发号问题误说成读写权限问题。
optionDirectness: 适合跨节点按时间排序的风险判断。
适合格式入门题，不适合分布式排序。
适合对比 vector clock 时说明边界。
不适合任何发号机制选择。
optionScenarioImpacts: ID 可能重复或顺序违反因果。
没有解释 clock skew 风险。
系统仍不知道完整 happened-before。
数据库写入能力不受该机制改变。
why: 物理时间不是分布式事实，它只是本机读数。clock drift 和回拨会让“更大的 timestamp”不一定代表更晚的因果事件。
why_en: Physical time is a local reading, so drift and rollback can make timestamp order disagree with causal order.
tradeoff: 简单时间排序 vs 时钟不确定性

termDefinitions.meaning: timestamp 是某个时钟读数编码出的时间值，不等于全局真实发生顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A timestamp is an encoded clock reading, not a guaranteed global event order.

termDefinitions.meaning: clock drift 是机器时钟随着时间逐渐偏离真实时间或其他机器时钟的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Clock drift is the gradual deviation of a machine clock from true time or other machine clocks.

termDefinitions.meaning: clock rollback 是本地时钟被校准到更早时间，可能让新事件拿到旧 timestamp。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Clock rollback is when a local clock is adjusted backward, so a new event can receive an older timestamp.

termDefinitions.meaning: NTP 是网络时间同步协议，用来校准机器时钟但不能消除所有误差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP is the Network Time Protocol, used to synchronize clocks but not eliminate all uncertainty.

termDefinitions.meaning: vector clock 是记录每个节点版本计数的因果元数据，不是物理时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector clock is causal metadata with per-node version counters, not physical time.

scenario: 一个发号器只用 UNIX 毫秒 timestamp 当 ID。毫秒粒度最多 1,000 个不同时间点/秒，也就是 86,400,000 个/天；需求是 ≥1,000,000,000 个/天。
scenario_en: An ID generator uses only a UNIX millisecond timestamp as the ID. Millisecond granularity gives at most 1,000 time slots per second, or 86,400,000 per day, while the requirement is at least 1,000,000,000 per day.
q: 为什么单纯 timestamp 不够？
q_en: Why is a timestamp-only ID not enough?
options: 同一毫秒内的并发事件会撞 ID，日容量也低于需求
timestamp 永远不能转换成数字
timestamp 自动包含 worker id 和 sequence
timestamp 天然解决所有 clock skew
options_en: Concurrent events in the same millisecond collide, and daily capacity is below the requirement.
A timestamp can never be represented as a number.
A timestamp automatically contains worker id and sequence fields.
A timestamp naturally solves all clock skew.
why: 公式是 1,000 slots/s × 86,400s/day = 86.4 million/day，小于 1 billion/day。并发事件共享同一毫秒时，还需要 worker id 和 sequence 来避免重复。
why_en: A millisecond timestamp gives only 86.4 million slots per day, and concurrent events need extra fields to avoid collisions.

q: Twitter Snowflake 的 64-bit ID 如何分段？
q_en: How is a Twitter Snowflake 64-bit ID laid out?
text: Snowflake 常见布局是 1 个 sign bit、{{41-bit timestamp}}、{{10-bit worker}}、{{12-bit sequence}}。
text_en: A common Snowflake layout is 1 sign bit, {{41-bit timestamp}}, {{10-bit worker}}, and {{12-bit sequence}}.
why: timestamp 负责大体时间排序，worker 区分发号节点，sequence 解决同一 worker 同一毫秒内的并发。12-bit sequence 表示每 worker 每毫秒最多 4096 个序号。
why_en: Timestamp gives time order, worker id separates generators, and sequence handles multiple IDs per worker per millisecond.
codeSample:
0 | 41-bit timestamp | 10-bit worker | 12-bit sequence
# 10-bit worker: 1024 workers
# 12-bit sequence: 4096 IDs per worker per ms

scenario: 你需要高可用、64-bit、按时间大致可排序的 ID；业务能接受依赖机器时钟，但要知道 NTP 回拨风险。
scenario_en: You need highly available 64-bit IDs that are roughly time-sortable, and the business accepts physical-clock dependence with rollback risk.
q: Snowflake 为什么合适但不是完美？
q_en: Why is Snowflake suitable but not perfect?
options: 它本地发号且时间可排序，但时钟漂移会破坏顺序或唯一性
它每个 ID 都要访问中心数据库，吞吐很低
它只能生成 128-bit 字符串
它完整记录每个节点的因果历史
options_en: It issues IDs locally and sorts by time, but clock drift can break order or uniqueness.
It must call a central database for every ID, so throughput is low.
It can only generate 128-bit strings.
It records full causal history for every node.
why: Snowflake 把 timestamp、worker 和 sequence 拼在一个 64-bit 数里，所以没有中心发号瓶颈。它的弱点是物理时间：未来时间、回拨和漂移都要额外防护。
why_en: Snowflake avoids central coordination with timestamp, worker, and sequence fields, but physical-clock problems still need safeguards.
whenOtherWins: 如果你必须证明跨地域因果顺序，TrueTime 或逻辑时钟方案比普通 Snowflake 更强。
tradeoff: 本地高吞吐发号 vs 物理时钟风险

q: Lamport clock 的更新时间规则是什么？
q_en: What is the update rule for a Lamport clock?
steps: 接收方收到消息后，把本地 clock 设为 max(local, received)+1
进程在本地事件前先把 counter 加一
发送消息时，把当前 counter 附在消息上
若 a happened-before b，则 timestamp(a) 小于 timestamp(b)
相同 timestamp 可用 node id 打破并列，形成任意 total order
why: Lamport clock 维护的是 happened-before 的必要顺序：消息接收一定晚于发送。它能给一致的偏序扩展，但不能单靠两个数字判断谁导致了谁。
why_en: Lamport clocks preserve happened-before ordering through message timestamps, but two values alone do not prove causality.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lamport clock 是用单调 counter 表示分布式事件偏序的逻辑时钟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Lamport clock is a logical counter used to preserve partial ordering of distributed events.

scenario: 两个事件的 Lamport timestamps 分别是 7 和 9，你只看到这两个数字和节点 ID，没有消息链路上下文。
scenario_en: Two events have Lamport timestamps 7 and 9, and you only see these values plus node IDs, without the message history.
q: 能否据此判断 7 导致了 9？
q_en: Can you conclude that timestamp 7 caused timestamp 9?
options: 不能；Lamport 保证因果会递增，但递增不反推出因果
能；数字小的一定是数字大的直接原因
能；只要 node id 更小就代表父事件
不能；Lamport timestamps 完全不支持排序
options_en: No; Lamport guarantees causality implies increasing time, but increasing time does not imply causality.
Yes; the smaller number is always the direct cause of the larger one.
Yes; the smaller node id always means parent event.
No; Lamport timestamps support no ordering at all.
why: Lamport 的方向是 a→b 则 L(a)<L(b)，但 L(a)<L(b) 可能只是并发事件被任意排了先后。要判断完整因果，需要 vector clock 或消息历史。
why_en: Lamport order is one-way evidence: causality increases clocks, but a larger clock does not prove causality.
tradeoff: 轻量偏序信号 vs 完整因果可判定

scenario: 你希望 ID 自身完整表达事件因果，但系统有大量客户端和服务节点，不能让每个 ID 带上所有节点的 counter。
scenario_en: You want the ID itself to encode full causality, but the system has many clients and service nodes, so each ID cannot carry every node counter.
q: vector-clock ID 的主要问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main problem with vector-clock-based IDs?
options: 它能表达因果，但状态大小随节点数增长，难塞进紧凑 ID
它无法判断任何并发冲突
它必须依赖 GPS 和原子钟
它只能生成完全随机的 128-bit 字符串
options_en: It captures causality, but state grows with node count and is hard to fit into compact IDs.
It cannot detect any concurrent conflict.
It requires GPS and atomic clocks.
It can only generate fully random 128-bit strings.
why: vector clock 的强项是完整因果，弱点是每个参与者都要一个 counter。节点数一多，ID 长度和更新成本都会压过 64-bit 紧凑目标。
why_en: Vector clocks capture full causality, but their per-node counters grow too large for compact 64-bit IDs.
whenOtherWins: 如果节点集合很小且因果判定比 ID 紧凑更重要，vector clock 很有价值。
tradeoff: 完整因果表达 vs ID 大小和可扩展性

scenario: 全球系统需要 64-bit、可扩展、高可用 ID，还希望在可证明的时间不确定性范围内维护因果顺序；团队能承担 GPS 和原子钟运维复杂度。
scenario_en: A global system needs scalable, highly available 64-bit IDs and wants causal ordering within a bounded time uncertainty model; the team can operate GPS and atomic clocks.
q: 为什么 TrueTime 类方案更强？
q_en: Why is a TrueTime-like scheme stronger?
options: 它返回时间区间和不确定性，只有区间不重叠时才断言顺序
它完全不需要任何物理时钟
它让所有事件都共享一个随机 UUID
它要求每次发号都锁住全局单行
options_en: It returns a time interval and uncertainty, and asserts order only when intervals do not overlap.
It needs no physical clocks at all.
It gives every event the same random UUID.
It locks one global row for every issued ID.
why: TrueTime 不假装本机 timestamp 就是真实时间点，而是给出 [earliest, latest] 区间。区间不重叠时才能安全排序，代价是硬件和运维复杂。
why_en: TrueTime models clock uncertainty explicitly with intervals, giving safe ordering when intervals do not overlap.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是需要大致时间排序，Snowflake 成本低得多。
tradeoff: 可证明时间顺序 vs 硬件运维成本

termDefinitions.meaning: TrueTime 是 Spanner 使用的时间 API，返回真实时间所在的区间而不是单点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TrueTime is Spanner's time API that returns an interval containing the true time rather than one timestamp.

termDefinitions.meaning: GPS 可提供高精度时间来源，TrueTime 类系统用它辅助约束时钟误差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GPS is the Global Positioning System and can provide precise time signals for bounding clock uncertainty.

q: TrueTime 类 64-bit ID 可以如何编码不确定性？
q_en: How can a TrueTime-like 64-bit ID encode uncertainty?
text: 一种布局是 41-bit timestamp、{{4-bit uncertainty}}、10-bit worker 和 8-bit sequence；uncertainty 表示时间区间宽度。
text_en: One layout is a 41-bit timestamp, {{4-bit uncertainty}}, 10-bit worker, and 8-bit sequence; uncertainty represents the interval width.
why: timestamp 给排序主轴，uncertainty 让比较方知道这不是精确单点。8-bit sequence 表示每 worker 每个时间粒度 256 个本地序号。
why_en: The timestamp gives the main order, while the uncertainty bits expose the width of the time interval.
codeSample:
41-bit earliest_time | 4-bit epsilon | 10-bit worker | 8-bit sequence
# order is safe only when A.latest < B.earliest

scenario: 事件 A 的 TrueTime 区间是 [100,108]，事件 B 的区间是 [105,112]；两个区间重叠。
scenario_en: Event A has TrueTime interval [100,108], and event B has interval [105,112]; the intervals overlap.
q: 能否安全断言 A 早于 B？
q_en: Can you safely assert that A happened before B?
options: 不能；区间重叠时真实时间可能交叉
能；A 的 earliest 比 B 小就足够
能；只要 B 的 latest 更大就足够
不能；TrueTime 从不支持任何排序
options_en: No; overlapping intervals mean the true times could cross.
Yes; A's earliest being smaller is enough.
Yes; B's latest being larger is enough.
No; TrueTime never supports any ordering.
why: TrueTime 的安全判断是 A_latest < B_earliest。这里只是 108 和 105 重叠，所以系统不能用时间证明先后。
why_en: The safe TrueTime rule is A_latest < B_earliest, and overlapping intervals do not prove order.
tradeoff: 安全排序断言 vs 不确定区间等待

scenario: 团队想用 Spanner 里单行 read-modify-write 生成严格全局递增序列，所有业务事件都必须排成一个总序。
scenario_en: A team wants to use a single-row read-modify-write in Spanner to generate a strictly globally increasing sequence for all business events.
q: 严格全局顺序的成本是什么？
q_en: What is the cost of strict global ordering?
options: 中心化更新会成为吞吐瓶颈，可能只有百 ops/s 量级
它会让所有写入自动分散到无限多热点
它比本地 Snowflake 更高可用且无任何等待
它会把 64-bit ID 空间缩小到 10 个值
options_en: The centralized update becomes a throughput bottleneck, potentially around hundreds of ops per second.
It automatically spreads every write across infinitely many hotspots.
It is more available than local Snowflake and needs no waiting.
It shrinks the 64-bit ID space to 10 values.
why: 严格总序通常要把所有事件挤过同一个协调点或同一行状态。放松为大致时间顺序或只保留必要因果，吞吐会高很多。
why_en: Strict global order usually funnels events through one coordination point, so relaxing order can dramatically improve throughput.
tradeoff: 严格总序 vs 发号吞吐

scenario: 分布式数据库按主键范围分片。你使用严格递增 ID，所有新写入都落在当前最大 ID 附近。
scenario_en: A distributed database shards by primary-key range. You use strictly increasing IDs, so every new write lands near the current maximum ID.
q: 单调递增 ID 会带来什么风险？
q_en: What risk do monotonically increasing IDs create?
options: 新写入集中到最后一个 range，形成写热点
每个 range 的写入会天然完全均匀
ID 越大，value 会自动变小
数据库不再需要复制
options_en: New writes concentrate on the last range and create a write hotspot.
Writes become perfectly balanced across all ranges.
The larger the ID, the smaller the value becomes.
The database no longer needs replication.
why: 范围分片看的是 key 的位置，递增 ID 会让最新写入总追着尾部 range 跑。可以用打散位、预分裂或非严格顺序方案缓解。
why_en: Range sharding sends increasing IDs to the tail range, creating a write hotspot unless the keyspace is spread out.
tradeoff: 按 ID 扫描友好 vs 写入均衡

q: 选择分布式 ID 方案时通常要同时检查哪些维度？
q_en: Which dimensions should you check when choosing a distributed ID scheme?
options: 唯一性：重复 ID 会造成支付、主键或追踪错误
紧凑性：大 key 会增加索引和存储成本
顺序语义：是否需要时间排序或因果排序
颜色语义：ID 字符串是否看起来更美观
options_en: Uniqueness: duplicate IDs can break payments, primary keys, or tracing.
Compactness: large keys increase index and storage cost.
Ordering semantics: whether time order or causal order is required.
Color semantics: whether the ID string looks visually nicer.
why: ID 不是只要“不重复”就结束，还会影响索引大小、写热点、范围扫描和调试链路。外观美观不是系统设计约束。
why_en: ID design affects uniqueness, index cost, hotspots, scans, and tracing, not just whether the string looks nice.
